FHSA contribution timing: draw the room, the deposits and the balance

Explore a simplified new-account calendar with four graphics that separate annual participation room, capped contributions and investment growth.

Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Ordinary-case illustration under FHSA participation rules reviewed 25 October 2026: first account opens in year 1, initial room CAD 8,000, annual base CAD 8,000, participation-room carryforward capped at CAD 8,000 and ordinary lifetime capacity CAD 40,000. Eligibility throughout the modeled years is assumed. Contributions arrive at year-end; existing balance earns the selected annual return. The central idea

Contribution room and account value measure different things. Track the opening year, usable room and actual deposits before projecting a home-saving balance.

01

Know the case the calendar is modeling

The CRA’s FHSA participation guidance gives CAD 8,000 of room in the year the first account opens. In the ordinary case illustrated here, subsequent room reflects the annual base, participation-room carryforward capped at CAD 8,000, and remaining ordinary lifetime capacity of CAD 40,000.

The model assumes the first FHSA opens in year one and the person remains eligible throughout the selected horizon. There are no prior accounts, RRSP transfers, withdrawals, excess amounts, designated amounts or re-participation adjustments. Those omissions matter because the full CRA calculation covers more situations.

The waiting input means an already open account receives no requested contributions for the initial years. It does not mean that the opening date is postponed. Room does not accumulate before the first account is opened, and opening also starts the maximum participation period, which this calculator does not determine.

02

Follow annual room before each deposit

The room chart compares available participation room with the contribution actually modeled each year. A requested deposit is limited to available room, and remaining ordinary lifetime capacity is checked separately. Requests that do not fit are recorded as unplaced cash rather than deposited as excess contributions.

The default account waits two years before requesting CAD 10,000 annually. It has CAD 8,000 of room in year one and CAD 16,000 in year two. Another unused year does not make the ordinary carryforward unlimited. The modeled year-three room remains CAD 16,000.

The first CAD 10,000 deposit leaves carryforward that supports room of CAD 14,000 in year four. The next selected deposits gradually use that carryforward. By the end of year six, cumulative deposits reach CAD 40,000, after which the ordinary lifetime constraint stops further modeled deposits.

03

Keep unplaced cash distinct from the FHSA balance

Across the default eight-year horizon, six annual requests of CAD 10,000 total CAD 60,000. The simplified calendar places CAD 40,000 in the account and records CAD 20,000 of requests that did not fit. The tool does not invest that unplaced amount elsewhere or include it in the account-value curve.

This cap is a convention of the illustration. It does not check contributions or transfers made in actual accounts. Participation room applies across the holder’s FHSAs; opening another account does not supply a separate copy of the same room. Reconcile actual transactions and the applicable CRA calculations before depositing.

The model also does not calculate a deduction or refund. The CRA’s FHSA overview distinguishes generally deductible contributions from RRSP-to-FHSA transfers, which are not deductible. Account room, deductible amounts and account value should not be treated as interchangeable figures.

04

Separate contributions from investment growth

Contributions arrive at year-end in this model. The existing balance first earns the selected annual return, then the allowed deposit is added. Under the default 4% assumption, the eight-year ending balance is CAD 45,929.75 from CAD 40,000 of contributions.

The waterfall separates those contributions from modeled growth or loss. Investment income generally does not consume participation room, so an account value above CAD 40,000 does not by itself show excess contributions. Conversely, a lower balance after an investment loss does not reopen contribution capacity in this ordinary model.

The comparison path removes the initial waiting period while keeping the same opening year, requested annual amount, return and finish date. Annual limits can change the actual deposit schedule, so this is a comparison of funding timing and constraints rather than investment performance.

05

Use the calendar alongside the actual account rules

The matrix varies the requested annual amount and the first contribution year, while retaining the selected finish date. Its cells show cumulative deposits that fit, not investment balances or tax deductions. They therefore remain unchanged when the investment-return input changes.

The calendar freezes the reviewed rules for a hypothetical horizon. It does not determine eligibility to open, maximum participation deadlines, qualifying withdrawals, account closure, transfers out, tax on excesses or the treatment of any actual account history. Confirm those details in current CRA guidance and your records.

A first-home plan also needs a purchase budget, closing costs, cash accessibility and an investment-risk review tied to the intended use date. Keep that wider funding need separate from the amount a registered account permits you to contribute. The four graphics explain the ordinary calendar without turning it into a personal room statement or a recommendation to open an account.
